newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares rise steadily in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares rise steadily in moderate trade.

text.p: Leading stocks maintained their steady appreciation in Nigerian share trading on Monday, propelled by growing investor-interest, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 7289.94 from 7268.28 on Friday.
"Stocks are currently enjoying a good run because of the 1997 budget which was generally acclaimed to be good for the market," said one dealer.

"Some shares, especially in the banking and insurance sectors, are receiving attention from investors buying on the expectation of capital appreciation because investors consider them cheap at their current prices," he added.
First Bank, Union Bank and FSB closed at 89.27 naira, 8.10 naira and 6.60 naira, adding seven kobo, eight kobo and 10 kobo, respectively.

Good performances kept demand for food shares up, benefiting Nestle which ended at 55.50 naira, up 40 kobo. Nigerian Bottling Company finished at 35.90 naira, up 20 kobo, the same gain as Union Dicon Salt which closed at 45.21 naira.

Mixed fortunes ruled cement and conglomerates. While West African Portland Cement added 20 kobo to 52.80 naira, Acacia Cement fell 10 kobo to 14.00 naira. UAC gained 15 kobo to 8.90 naira but John Holt slumped by 10 kobo to 9.60 naira.
Oil marketers, led by Unipetrol, closed 30 kobo higher at 66.70 naira, National Oil gained 25 kobo to 52.85 naira and African Petroleum was 20 kobo firmer at 50.50 naira.
Guinness fell five kobo to 7.95 naira but Afprint and National Salt Company lost one kobo each at 2.48 naira and 6.29 naira.
But improved perception of tyre maker Dunlop earned the stock a 15 kobo rise, closing at 8.05 naira.
